title: grpc-webnext conformance case file
description: A suite of scenarios run by a client driver against a ConformanceService server. See conformance/README.md.

suite.description: Suite name; matches the file stem.

bytes.description: A byte value: UTF-8 text, base64, or N zero bytes (for size-limit cases).

b64.description: For -bin keys; base64 of the binary value.

rest.description: Drive this case as a raw google.api.http REST call instead of an RPC through the client. The URL is the route, so `rpc` only selects the transport the spec mandates: a unary method's annotation URL is Fetch, a streaming method's (including client-streaming) is a WebSocket. Always JSON, so `codecs`/`transports` do not apply and the case runs exactly once. `cancel_after_messages` is NOT honored on a REST case — synthesizing CANCELLED locally is client behavior, and this driver is deliberately not a client.

verb.description: HTTP method. Ignored on the WebSocket surface, where an upgrade is always a GET and matching is verb-agnostic.

path.description: Annotation URL including any query string, e.g. "/v1/rest-stream/hi?count=3".

body.description: Raw JSON request body — one request message. Omit for a body-less (GET-style) binding. Mutually exclusive with `bodies`.

bodies.description: Several raw JSON request messages, for a client-streaming or bidi annotation route: the first opens the stream, the rest follow as message frames, then the driver half-closes. WebSocket surface only — a Fetch REST call carries exactly one body. Mutually exclusive with `body`.

content_type.description: Override the request content-type (Fetch) or the offered subprotocol (WebSocket). Default: plain `application/json` on Fetch, a blank subprotocol on WebSocket — the surfaces a browser reaches an annotated URL with. Set it to a wrong-surface value to exercise rejection.

transports.description: Run the case once per listed transport. Default: Unary -> [fetch, websocket]; streaming -> [websocket].

codecs.description: Run the case once per listed codec (cartesian with transports). Default [proto, json].

timeout_millis.description: grpc-timeout the client sets on the call. The client also enforces this locally, so a passing case does NOT prove the server did anything — use `header_timeout_millis` for that.

header_timeout_millis.description: Send `grpc-timeout` as a raw header WITHOUT arming the client's own deadline timer, so only the server can end the call. This is how server-side deadline enforcement is observed; with `timeout_millis` the client's timer fires first and masks the server. Unary only — a streaming call on the custom `Frame` path carries its deadline in the envelope, not a header.

request_metadata.description: Request headers the driver attaches to the call.

requires.description: Server config profile this case needs (e.g. max_message_bytes, transcoder). The harness selects a matching server; an unsatisfiable profile marks the case SKIPPED.

cancel_after_messages.description: Client resets/cancels the stream after receiving N messages (drives Reset propagation).

http_status.description: Assert a raw HTTP status rather than a gRPC one — for surface rejections that never become an RPC (e.g. `+proto` on a REST URL is 415). REST cases only; a WebSocket rejection carries a `4000 + code` close, so it is asserted as an ordinary `status.code`.

not_ok.description: Assert any non-OK status (rejection), when the exact code is transport-dependent.

raw_body.description: REST only: assert the response body VERBATIM, as JSON text. Needed when the body is not the RPC's response message — `response_body` makes it a bare field value, which no message matcher can express.

raw_messages.description: REST/WebSocket twin of `raw_body`: assert each streamed message's JSON verbatim.

received_count.description: ClientStream only: how many request messages the server reports having received (ClientStreamResponse.received_count). Without this, a client-streaming case proves nothing about messages after the first — the response payload comes from the FIRST request's ResponseDefinition either way.
